coverage_changes.change: Repaired the existing query: optional comment quantification between two anchors missed plain import(variable). Separate plain and leading-comment patterns now match identifiers and property/index lookups. Negative controls reject literal imports with an options argument, comments, strings, method names and erased import types.
coverage_changes.consumer_check: All hostile, benign, obfuscation and reverse-shell regression groups pass; complete DMG and extracted module scans have no suspicious or hostile traits.

coverage_changes.change: New AST matcher binds add and a recognized dependency saveType to the same reify call argument. It accepts reversed and quoted option keys without depending on receiver variable names. It does not prove receiver identity or installation success.
New AST matcher recognizes true and minified !0 lifecycle-script suppression options. It records requested configuration, not enforcement, and does not imply imported JavaScript cannot execute.

New literal matcher recognizes /api/config and versioned /api/vN/config paths with static or computed origins. The description claims an endpoint-path reference rather than a remote fetch or code-delivery flow.
New source-banner observation records bytecode compilation annotations. Quoted text and near-miss annotation names are negative controls. No claim is made that bytecode was independently examined.

reference_audit.exact_consumers: All four relocated observations have their explicit consumers updated; retired IDs are absent from the final DMG report.
reference_audit.directory_selectors: Weak common/test text was placed outside metadata/package/testing to avoid widening broad test exclusions. The native marker remains runtime identity with mapped-section and size bounds; real-framework identity and its quarantine exclusion were checked separately.
reference_audit.negative_control: A quoted common-helper example emits source-syntax metadata and no metadata/package/testing findings.
reference_audit.placement_contract: TAXONOMY.md documents the boundary between source-text syntax and a proven test-harness role.

future_triage: Computed loading, API configuration paths and programmatic installation now remain visible when an attacker renames variables, changes the server host/API version, reverses option order, or avoids npm shell commands. These are neutral evidence for comparison and investigation; their coexistence does not establish malicious remote configuration or credential exfiltration.
remaining_analysis_limits: The outer scanner recognizes the Bun Mach-O section but does not automatically enumerate this embedded module graph. The 612-entry graph and nested Brotli assets still required the separate extraction described in reverse-engineering.json. These YAML changes do not repair that engine extraction gap.
The bytecode banner is a build annotation, not proof of semantic equivalence between cached bytecode and extracted source.
Configuration-to-package-to-credential behavior spans modules and cannot be established by these atomic matchers. No hostile rule was added from same-file co-occurrence or OpenCode branding.
